'''William M. Kantor''' (born September 19, 1944) is an American mathematician who works in [[finite group|finite group theory]] and [[finite geometry|finite geometries]], particularly in computational aspects of these subjects.

==Education and career==
Kantor graduated with a bachelor's degree from [[Brooklyn College]] in 1964.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.linkedin.com/in/william-kantor-001b0199 |title=William Kantor |publisher=[[LinkedIn]] }}</ref>  He went on to graduate studies at the [[University of Wisconsin]], receiving his PhD in 1968 under the supervision of [[Peter Dembowski]] and [[R. H. Bruck]].<ref name=mathgenealogy>{{MathGenealogy|id=9059|name=William M. Kantor}}</ref>  He then worked at the [[University of Illinois at Chicago]] from 1968 to 1971 before moving in 1971 to the [[University of Oregon]], where he remained for the rest of his career.

Kantor's research mostly involves [[finite group]]s, often in relation to [[finite geometry|finite geometries]] and [[Computational group theory|computation]].  Algorithms developed by him have found use, for example, in the [[GAP (computer algebra system)|GAP]] computer algebra system.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gap-system.org|title=GAP source code|website=Official GAP system website|access-date=September 27, 2019}}</ref>
<!-- Missing Oberwolfach and Ohio State conference, which I don't think are highly notable -->

Kantor has written over 170 papers,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet/search/author.html?mrauthid=97975 |title=William Kantor author profile|website=[[MathSciNet]]|publisher=American Mathematical Society|url-access=subscription}}</ref> and has advised 7 PhD students.<ref name=mathgenealogy />

==Awards and honors==
* In 2013, Kantor was named a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] as a member of the inaugural class of fellows.<ref>{{cite journal |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date= May 2013 |title=Fellows of the AMS: Inaugural Class |url=http://www.ams.org/profession/ams-fellows/rnoti-p631.pdf |journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society |volume=60 |issue=5 |pages=631–637 |access-date=September 24, 2019}}</ref>
* In 2004, a conference "Finite geometries, groups, and computation" was held in honor of Kantor's 60th birthday.<ref name="Hulpke 2006 p. ">{{cite book | editor1-last=Hulpke | editor1-first=Alexander | editor2-last=Liebler | editor2-first=Robert | editor3-last=Penttila | editor3-first=Tim | editor4-last=Seress | editor4-first=Ákos | title=Finite geometries, groups, and computation | publisher=Walter de Gruyter | location=Berlin New York | year=2006 | isbn=978-3-11-019974-1 | oclc=181078514 | mr=2256928}}</ref>
* In 1998, Kantor gave an invited talk at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Berlin.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.emis.de/mirror/ICM98/B/3/2/|title=Invited Lectures in Algebra at the Berlin ICM|access-date=September 24, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|author=Kantor, William M.|chapter=Simple groups in computational group theory|title=Doc. Math. (Bielefeld) Extra Vol. ICM Berlin, 1998, vol. II|year=1998|pages=77–86|chapter-url=https://www.elibm.org/ft/10011643000}}</ref>
